clue.text: Won't it give you a free ride?

definitions.text: Won't it give you a free ride?

parts.words: Won't it give you a free ride?
parts.note: a war horse carries its rider, yet the word also names someone who bills you, so no ride from that sort comes free

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether something offers a lift without payment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question plays on two senses: a horse that carries a knight, and a person who charges a fee and so gives nothing for free.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a cavalry or war horse, which gives its rider a ride.

clue.text: Proviso for Santa to head East

indicators.note: Santa is told to go at the front, so his name heads the letter for East

parts.note: Santa Claus, the Christmas gift-bringer
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A condition requiring Father Christmas to set off eastwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause in a contract is a stipulation or condition, i.e. a proviso.

clue.text: Greek god's head set in a ring

indicators.note: the word for head is placed inside the letters from 'a ring'

parts.note: taken as written
O is ring-shaped
poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax

explanation.surface: A statue's head of a Greek deity mounted in a circular setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek deity of music, poetry and the sun.

clue.text: Craftsmen do in G & S role, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters before it may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Skilled artisans perhaps taking part in a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of DO IN G and S ROLE; the ampersand gives no letters. 'Craftsmen' means men who handle a craft, a boat, not artisans.
explanation.definitionFit: Gondoliers row gondolas, so they are boatmen in charge of a craft, a pun on artisans.

clue.text: From old-timer I'd get a wrinkle

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, spanning several of them

explanation.surface: An elderly person explaining they would acquire a line on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a raised line or crease on a surface, much like a wrinkle.

clue.text: Settled for having team in scarlet

indicators.note: the team word is placed inside the colour word

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Someone settled down because they had a team playing in red kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resided somewhere is to have lived or settled there.

clue.text: It's revolting, drive away fast!

parts.note: to repel an attacker is to drive them away
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A cry that something disgusting is nearby, so chase it off quickly!
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as 'quickly', but it is the noun: LENT, the forty-day fast before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent is disgusting or causes aversion, a synonym of revolting.

clue.text: Place to view, we hear

indicators.note: signals a word with the same pronunciation as the one meaning something to look at

parts.note: a sight is something worth looking at

explanation.surface: A spot for sightseeing, as people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or plot, i.e. a place.

clue.text: Girl's taking position as cashier

parts.note: Di is a girl's short name, with the possessive giving DI'S
a place is a position

explanation.surface: A young woman getting a job working the till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cashier' looks like a noun for a till worker, but here it is the verb meaning to dismiss from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them, and to displace someone is to remove them from their post.

clue.text: The last thing a crowd will do

definitions.text: The last thing a crowd will do

parts.words: The last thing a crowd will do
parts.note: looks like something a crowd would never do, but means what it finally does at the end of an event

explanation.surface: Something a crowd would never dream of doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last thing' idiomatically means 'least likely', but read literally it is the final act: at the end, a crowd breaks up and goes home.
explanation.definitionFit: When an event ends, the crowd scatters and goes its separate ways.

clue.text: A grain that's seen only in oak

parts.note: taken as written
corn is grain

explanation.surface: A cereal said to occur only in a particular tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak tree, found on no other tree.

clue.text: Delegates sort out dispute with Middle West

indicators.note: to sort out is to rearrange, so the letters of 'dispute' are shuffled
the central letters are taken from the word that follows

explanation.surface: Representatives resolving a quarrel involving the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort out' rearranges DISPUTE into DEPUTIS; 'Middle' takes ES, the centre of WEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deputises acts on another's behalf, as a delegate does; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Bacterium may be found on all meals badly cooked

indicators.note: food spoiled in the kitchen suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A germ that lurks on all poorly prepared dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmonella is a genus of bacteria behind food poisoning.

clue.text: Frozen field left in the grip of the enemy

indicators.note: the letter for left is held inside the word for enemy

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: An icy battlefield abandoned to opposing forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A floe is a sheet of floating sea ice, a frozen expanse like a field.

clue.text: Safe place in a bank?

parts.note: a safe is kept in a secure vault in a bank, and the room for it is a fortified one

explanation.surface: Asking where a bank keeps its valuables secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' reads as an adjective, but also suggests the noun: the room where a bank's safes are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongroom is a fortified vault where a bank keeps valuables.

clue.text: Messes about with examiner's marks? Nonsense

parts.note: to fiddle with something is to mess about with it
an examiner puts ticks beside correct answers

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with exam scores, and the accusation is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old exclamation meaning rubbish or stuff and nonsense.

clue.text: Boxer takes on contests at a higher level

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
to take on an opponent is to fight them

explanation.surface: A pugilist moves up to bouts in a higher division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' looks like a fighter, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogfights are aerial combats between fighter planes, contests fought high in the sky.

clue.text: Cuts in diocese set up blackouts

indicators.note: the word for cuts goes inside the reversed word for diocese
in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
to clip is to cut

explanation.surface: Budget reductions within a church district create power outages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SEE into EES, which then holds CLIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse blots out the sun or moon, a natural blackout.

clue.text: Poor pun, drear and not up to scratch

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A feeble, dreary wordplay joke that fails to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling under par means below the normal standard, i.e. not up to scratch.

clue.text: Worshipful company?

parts.note: London livery companies are styled Worshipful, but the phrase can also mean a group of worshippers

explanation.surface: A reference to one of the City of London's livery guilds.
explanation.walkthrough: London's old trade guilds are titled 'The Worshipful Company of ...', which leads away from a church gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A congregation is a body of people assembled for worship.

clue.text: Writer, good man at heart, seen in French bar

indicators.note: the good man goes into the centre of the writer word

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes
St, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: An author with a virtuous heart spotted drinking in a Parisian bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is a pen: BIRO, the British name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small French café-bar or restaurant.

clue.text: Meet Di and Joan when out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or turned out of place

explanation.surface: Two women arranging to get together on a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that adjoin meet at a shared border.

clue.text: Fancy a little hideaway

indicators.note: only a small part of the word is taken, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Liking the idea of a small secluded retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy can mean a notion or thought, which an idea is.

clue.text: What you face in the teeth of a gale?

definitions.text: What you face in the teeth of a gale?

parts.words: What you face in the teeth of a gale?
parts.note: in the teeth of means directly against, and teeth also suggest biting

explanation.surface: Asking what one meets when walking straight into a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting wind is a bitterly cold, piercing one, the kind met heading into a gale.

clue.text: Me to serve? Perfect!

parts.note: the speaker of the clue refers to themselves as I
to deal cards is to serve them out

explanation.surface: Delighted at being asked to wait at table.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless or perfect.

clue.text: Left in cooler, it may get jammed

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the cooler word

parts.note: a fan cools you down

explanation.surface: Something left in a cold box might get stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jammed' suggests stuck, but a flan can be filled with jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry tart, which may be filled with jam.

clue.text: Lush crepe put round burial place

indicators.note: the letters are turned around and placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Luxurious crêpe fabric draped around a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a tomb, a place of burial.

clue.text: Beat unconscious, then execute!

parts.note: someone knocked out is out cold
to do a task is to execute it

explanation.surface: A violent instruction to knock someone senseless and then kill them.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo a rival is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: Contracts provided by psychiatrists

definitions.meaning: a verb, gets smaller in size
slang for mind doctors, short for headshrinkers

explanation.surface: Agreements supplied by mental health doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink is to get smaller, while shrinks is also slang for psychiatrists.

clue.text: Make fun of the French politician with nothing on

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine form
MP, Member of Parliament
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Mocking the French parliamentarian who wears nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to satirise or ridicule them.
